text: Python is a high-level programming language used for automation, AI, web development, data analysis, and scripting. It emphasizes readability and simplicity.
JavaScript is a programming language primarily used for web development. It runs in browsers and on servers via Node.js. It enables interactive web pages and dynamic content.
Variables are named containers that store data values in a program. They allow code to reference and manipulate data by name instead of by memory address.
Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform a specific task. They take inputs called parameters, process them, and may return a result. Functions enable code reuse and modularity.
Loops are control structures that repeat a block of code multiple times. Common loop types include for loops, while loops, and do-while loops. They automate repetitive tasks.
Conditions are statements that execute different code branches based on whether a boolean expression is true or false. If-else statements and switch cases are common condition structures.
Classes are templates for creating objects in object-oriented programming. They define properties and methods that all instances of the class share. Classes support encapsulation and inheritance.

APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) are sets of rules that allow software components to communicate. REST APIs use HTTP methods like GET and POST. APIs enable integration between different systems.
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a lightweight data format used for storing and exchanging data. It uses key-value pairs and arrays. JSON is language-independent and human-readable.
Algorithms are step-by-step procedures for solving problems. They take input, process it through defined steps, and produce output. Algorithm efficiency is measured by time and space complexity.

Data structures are organized ways of storing and accessing data. Common data structures include arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and hash tables. The choice of data structure affects performance.
Arrays are ordered collections of elements accessed by index. They provide O(1) random access but have fixed size in many languages. Arrays are fundamental data structures in programming.

Objects are instances of classes that combine data and behavior. They encapsulate state in properties and expose functionality through methods. Objects are the building blocks of object-oriented programming.

Compilation is the process of translating source code into machine code that a computer can execute. Compilers convert high-level languages like C++ into binary. Compiled programs run faster than interpreted ones.
Interpreters execute source code line by line without compiling it first. Languages like Python and JavaScript use interpreters. Interpreted code is more portable but slower than compiled code.

Error handling is the practice of anticipating and managing errors in code. Try-catch blocks catch exceptions and allow graceful recovery. Good error handling prevents crashes and improves user experience.

Libraries are collections of pre-written code that provide reusable functionality. They save developers time by offering tested implementations of common tasks. Examples include NumPy for Python and React for JavaScript.

Frameworks are structured platforms that provide a foundation for building applications. They define architecture, conventions, and tools. Examples include Django for Python and Angular for JavaScript.
Backend development refers to server-side programming that handles business logic, database operations, and API responses. Backend technologies include Python, Java, Go, and Node.js.
Frontend development refers to client-side programming that creates the user interface. Frontend technologies include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and frameworks like React and Vue.

Neural networks are computational models inspired by the human brain. They consist of layers of interconnected nodes that process input and produce output. Neural networks learn by adjusting weights during training.

Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence where computers learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed. It includes supervised learning (labeled data), unsupervised learning (unlabeled data), and reinforcement learning (reward-based). Machine learning is used for prediction, classification, recommendation, and automation.

Training data is the dataset used to teach a machine learning model. The model learns patterns from training data to make predictions on new data. Quality and quantity of training data affect model performance.
Inference is the process of using a trained model to make predictions on new data. It occurs after training is complete. Inference speed is important for real-time applications.

LLM (Large Language Model) is a type of AI model trained on vast text data to generate human-like text. LLMs use transformer architecture and predict the next token in a sequence. Examples include GPT and BERT.

Transformers are a neural network architecture that uses self-attention mechanisms. They process input sequences in parallel rather than sequentially. Transformers are the foundation of modern language models.

Embeddings are vector representations of data in a continuous space. They capture semantic relationships between items. Embeddings enable similarity search and are used in recommendation systems and NLP.

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) combines a knowledge base with a language model. It retrieves relevant documents and uses them as context for generation. RAG reduces hallucinations by grounding responses in facts.

AI agents are autonomous systems that perceive their environment and take actions to achieve goals. They use reasoning, planning, and tool use. Agents can operate independently or collaborate with other agents.

Fine-tuning is the process of adapting a pre-trained model to a specific task. It involves further training on task-specific data. Fine-tuning improves performance on specialized tasks while leveraging general knowledge.
Supervised learning is a machine learning approach where models learn from labeled data. Each training example has an input and a correct output. The model learns to map inputs to outputs.

Unsupervised learning is a machine learning approach where models find patterns in unlabeled data. Common techniques include clustering and dimensionality reduction. The model discovers structure without explicit guidance.

Reinforcement learning is a machine learning approach where an agent learns by interacting with an environment. It receives rewards or penalties for actions and learns a policy to maximize cumulative reward.

Classification is a supervised learning task that assigns inputs to discrete categories. Examples include spam detection and image recognition. The model learns decision boundaries from labeled training data.

Regression is a supervised learning task that predicts continuous numerical values. Examples include price prediction and temperature forecasting. The model learns the relationship between input features and output values.

Clustering is an unsupervised learning task that groups similar data points together. Common algorithms include k-means and hierarchical clustering. Clustering reveals natural structure in data without labels.

Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data too closely, including noise. It performs well on training data but poorly on new data. Regularization and cross-validation help prevent overfitting.

Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in data. It performs poorly on both training and test data. Increasing model complexity or features can address underfitting.

Model evaluation measures how well a model performs on unseen data. Common metrics include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Evaluation uses a separate test set to estimate real-world performance.

ML pipelines are sequences of data processing steps that transform raw data into trained models. They include data cleaning, feature engineering, model training, and evaluation. Pipelines ensure reproducibility and automation.

Vector search is a technique for finding similar items by comparing their vector embeddings. It uses similarity metrics like cosine similarity or Euclidean distance. Vector search powers recommendation systems and semantic search.

Vulnerabilities are weaknesses in software or systems that can be exploited by attackers. They arise from coding errors, misconfigurations, or design flaws. Identifying and patching vulnerabilities is critical for security.

CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) is a standardized identifier for known security vulnerabilities. Each CVE has a unique ID and description. CVEs enable consistent tracking and referencing of vulnerabilities.

CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) is a framework for rating the severity of security vulnerabilities. Scores range from 0 to 10. Higher scores indicate more severe vulnerabilities that should be prioritized.

EPSS (Exploit Prediction Scoring System) estimates the likelihood that a vulnerability will be exploited in the wild. Scores range from 0 to 1. EPSS helps prioritize patching by focusing on likely-to-be-exploited vulnerabilities.

Threats are potential events or actors that can exploit vulnerabilities to cause harm. Threats include hackers, malware, natural disasters, and insider attacks. Threat modeling helps identify and mitigate risks.

Exploits are techniques or code that take advantage of vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access or cause damage. Exploits can be remote or local, automated or manual. Zero-day exploits target unknown vulnerabilities.

Risk scoring in cybersecurity quantifies the potential impact and likelihood of security events. It combines threat likelihood, vulnerability severity, and asset value. Risk scores guide security investment decisions.

Firewalls are network security devices that filter traffic based on rules. They block unauthorized access while allowing legitimate traffic. Firewalls can be hardware or software and operate at network or application layers.

Encryption is the process of converting data into an unreadable format to protect confidentiality. Only authorized parties with the decryption key can read the data. Common algorithms include AES and RSA.
Authentication verifies the identity of a user or system. Common methods include passwords, tokens, biometrics, and multi-factor authentication. Strong authentication prevents unauthorized access.
Authorization determines what actions an authenticated user is allowed to perform. It enforces access control policies. Role-based access control (RBAC) is a common authorization model.

Penetration testing is the practice of simulating attacks on a system to find vulnerabilities. Ethical hackers use the same techniques as real attackers. Pen tests help organizations identify and fix security gaps.

Malware is malicious software designed to damage or gain unauthorized access to systems. Types include viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, and spyware. Antivirus software and behavioral detection help prevent malware infections.

Phishing is a social engineering attack where attackers impersonate trusted entities to steal credentials or information. Phishing attacks use fake emails, websites, or messages. User training and email filtering help prevent phishing.

Zero-day vulnerabilities are security flaws that are unknown to the vendor and have no patch available. They are highly valuable to attackers. Zero-day exploits can cause significant damage before they are discovered and fixed.

Patch management is the process of identifying, acquiring, and applying updates to software and systems. Timely patching closes known vulnerabilities. Automated patch management ensures consistent update deployment.

Incident response is the structured approach to handling security breaches. It includes detection, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident analysis. A well-defined incident response plan minimizes damage.

SOC (Security Operations Center) is a team that monitors and responds to security events. SOCs use SIEM tools to correlate alerts and identify threats. SOCs operate 24/7 to protect organizations from cyber attacks.

SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) is a platform that aggregates and analyzes security logs. It correlates events from multiple sources to detect threats. SIEM enables real-time threat detection and response.

Asset discovery is the process of identifying all hardware and software assets in an organization. It provides visibility into the attack surface. Asset inventories are essential for vulnerability management and compliance.
Atoms are the smallest units of matter that retain the properties of an element. They consist of protons, neutrons, and electrons. Atoms combine to form molecules through chemical bonds.
Molecules are groups of atoms bonded together. They are the smallest units of compounds. Water (H2O) is a molecule made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

Energy is the capacity to do work. It exists in forms including kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, and electrical. Energy can be transformed but not created or destroyed, according to the law of conservation of energy.

Force is a push or pull that acts on an object. It is measured in newtons. Forces can change the speed, direction, or shape of objects. Newton's laws describe the relationship between force and motion.
Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object. It is measured in kilograms. Mass is constant regardless of location, unlike weight which depends on gravity.

Gravity is the force that attracts objects with mass toward each other. It is responsible for keeping planets in orbit and objects on the ground. gravitational acceleration on Earth is approximately 9.8 m/s^2.

Electricity is the flow of electric charge through a conductor. It powers most modern technology. Electricity is measured in volts, amps, and watts. Circuits control the flow of electricity for practical use.
Magnetism is a force that attracts or repels magnetic materials. It is caused by moving electric charges. Electromagnets use electric current to create controllable magnetic fields.

Chemical reactions are processes where substances transform into new substances. Reactants are converted into products. Reactions involve breaking and forming chemical bonds. Examples include combustion and oxidation.
Cells are the basic structural and functional units of life. All living organisms are made of cells. Cells contain genetic material and perform processes like metabolism and reproduction.

DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the molecule that carries genetic information in living organisms. It has a double helix structure. DNA encodes the instructions for building proteins and determines inherited traits.

Evolution is the process by which species change over generations through natural selection. Organisms with advantageous traits survive and reproduce more successfully. Evolution explains the diversity of life on Earth.

Ecosystems are communities of living organisms interacting with their physical environment. They include producers, consumers, and decomposers. Ecosystems maintain balance through food webs and nutrient cycles.
Light is electromagnetic radiation visible to the human eye. It travels at approximately 300,000 km/s in a vacuum. Light behaves as both a wave and a particle (photon).

Sound is a mechanical wave that travels through a medium like air or water. It is caused by vibrations. Sound travels at different speeds in different materials. Humans hear sounds between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz.
Heat is thermal energy transferred between objects of different temperatures. It flows from hotter to cooler objects. Heat transfer occurs through conduction, convection, and radiation.
Pressure is force applied per unit area. It is measured in pascals. Atmospheric pressure is the weight of air above a point. Pressure differences cause weather patterns and fluid flow.
Motion is the change in position of an object over time. It is described by velocity, acceleration, and displacement. Newton's laws of motion govern the relationship between force and movement.
Space is the boundless three-dimensional extent in which all matter exists. It is studied in astronomy and cosmology. The universe contains galaxies, stars, planets, and other celestial bodies.

Time is a dimension in which events occur in sequence. It is measured in seconds, minutes, hours, and years. Time is relative according to Einstein's theory of relativity, meaning it can pass at different rates.
Money is a medium of exchange used to facilitate transactions. It serves as a unit of account and a store of value. Modern money includes physical currency and digital balances.
Currency is a system of money used in a particular country. Examples include the US dollar, Euro, and Norwegian krone. Exchange rates determine the value of one currency relative to another.

Loans are borrowed money that must be repaid with interest. They allow individuals and businesses to access funds before they have the full amount. Loan terms specify repayment schedule and interest rate.

Interest is the cost of borrowing money, expressed as a percentage of the loan amount. It is also the return on savings and investments. Simple interest is calculated on the principal, compound interest on principal plus accumulated interest.
Savings are money set aside for future use rather than immediate spending. Savings accounts earn interest. Building savings provides financial security and enables future investments.

Investments are assets purchased with the expectation of generating returns. Common investments include stocks, bonds, real estate, and mutual funds. All investments carry varying levels of risk and potential return.
Stocks represent ownership shares in a company. Stockholders may receive dividends and benefit from price appreciation. Stock prices fluctuate based on company performance and market conditions.

Bonds are debt securities where investors lend money to an entity for a fixed period. The issuer pays periodic interest and returns the principal at maturity. Bonds are generally less risky than stocks.

Accounts are records of financial transactions maintained by banks for their customers. Common types include checking accounts for daily transactions and savings accounts for storing money with interest.

Transactions are individual financial exchanges that move money between accounts. They include deposits, withdrawals, transfers, and payments. Transactions are recorded for tracking and auditing purposes.

Banking systems are networks of institutions that provide financial services. Banks accept deposits, make loans, and facilitate payments. Modern banking includes online and mobile banking for digital access.
Credit allows consumers to borrow money or access goods with a promise to pay later. Credit scores measure creditworthiness. Good credit enables lower interest rates and better loan terms.
Debit cards deduct money directly from a checking account for purchases. Unlike credit cards, they do not involve borrowing. Debit cards are linked to bank accounts and provide immediate payment.
Capital refers to financial assets or resources used to generate income. It can be cash, equipment, or investments. Capital is essential for business operations and growth.
Assets are resources owned by an individual or organization that have economic value. They include cash, property, equipment, and investments. Assets are listed on balance sheets.

Liabilities are financial obligations or debts owed by an individual or organization. They include loans, accounts payable, and mortgages. Liabilities are subtracted from assets to determine net worth.

Balance sheets are financial statements that show assets, liabilities, and equity at a point in time. They follow the equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Balance sheets provide a snapshot of financial position.

Accounting is the process of recording, classifying, and summarizing financial transactions. It provides information for decision-making and compliance. Accounting follows principles like GAAP or IFRS.

IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) are accounting standards issued by the IASB. They define how financial transactions are reported. IFRS aims for transparency and comparability across countries.

Financial statements are formal records of financial activities. They include the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement. Financial statements are used by investors, regulators, and management.
Countries are distinct geographical and political entities with their own governments. There are approximately 195 countries in the world. Each country has its own laws, culture, and economy.
Cities are large human settlements with significant population density. They serve as centers of commerce, culture, and governance. Major world cities include Tokyo, New York, London, and Paris.

Weather refers to short-term atmospheric conditions including temperature, precipitation, wind, and humidity. Weather is distinct from climate, which describes long-term patterns. Weather forecasting uses meteorological data and models.

Technology refers to the application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes. It includes tools, machines, software, and systems. Technology has transformed communication, transportation, healthcare, and entertainment.

The Internet is a global network of interconnected computers that communicate using standard protocols. It enables email, web browsing, file sharing, and real-time communication. The Internet has transformed access to information.
Computers are electronic devices that process data according to instructions. They consist of hardware components like CPU, memory, and storage. Computers run software programs to perform tasks.

Software is a set of instructions that tells a computer what to do. It includes operating systems, applications, and utilities. Software is written in programming languages and compiled or interpreted for execution.

Hardware refers to the physical components of a computer system. It includes the CPU, memory, storage devices, input devices, and output devices. Hardware works with software to perform computing tasks.
Networks are systems that connect computers and devices to share data and resources. They can be local (LAN) or wide area (WAN). Networks use protocols like TCP/IP to ensure reliable communication.

Data is information stored in a format suitable for processing by computers. It can be structured, semi-structured, or unstructured. Data is the foundation of analysis, machine learning, and decision-making.

Storage refers to the retention of digital data on physical or cloud-based media. Common storage types include hard drives, SSDs, and cloud storage. Storage capacity is measured in bytes, gigabytes, and terabytes.

Cloud computing delivers computing services over the internet. It includes storage, processing, databases, and software. Cloud providers include AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Cloud computing enables scalable and on-demand resources.
Servers are computers that provide services to other computers over a network. They host websites, databases, applications, and files. Servers are designed for reliability and continuous operation.
Websites are collections of web pages accessible via URLs. They are hosted on servers and viewed through browsers. Websites use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for structure, styling, and interactivity.
Browsers are software applications that retrieve and display web content. They interpret HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to render web pages. Popular browsers include Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

Email is a digital communication method for sending and receiving messages over the internet. It uses protocols like SMTP for sending and IMAP for receiving. Email is one of the most widely used communication tools.
Communication is the exchange of information between entities. Modern communication includes email, messaging, video calls, and social media. Technology has made communication instant and global.

Education is the process of acquiring knowledge, skills, and values. It occurs through formal schooling, self-study, and experience. Education is essential for personal development and economic opportunity.

Work refers to productive activity that produces goods or services. It is typically performed in exchange for wages. The nature of work has evolved with technology, enabling remote work and digital collaboration.

Society is a group of people living together in an organized community. It has structures for governance, economy, and culture. Societies develop norms, laws, and institutions to maintain order and cooperation.

Star Wars is a famous science fiction franchise created by George Lucas in 1977. It is set in a galaxy far, far away and follows the conflict between the Jedi and the Sith. The original trilogy includes A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, and Return of the Jedi. Star Wars is one of the highest-grossing film franchises of all time.

The Lord of the Rings is a fantasy franchise based on the novels by J.R.R. Tolkien. The film trilogy was directed by Peter Jackson and includes The Fellowship of the Ring, The Two Towers, and The Return of the King. It is widely considered one of the greatest film trilogies ever made, winning 17 Academy Awards.

Harry Potter is a fantasy franchise based on the book series by J.K. Rowling. It follows a young wizard named Harry Potter and his friends at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. The film series spans 8 movies and is one of the highest-grossing franchises in cinema history.

Marvel is a media franchise featuring superheroes from Marvel Comics. The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) includes characters like Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Spider-Man, and the Avengers. It is the highest-grossing film franchise of all time with over 30 interconnected films.

Star Trek is a science fiction franchise created by Gene Roddenberry in 1966. It follows the crew of the starship Enterprise as they explore the galaxy. The franchise includes multiple TV series and films, and is known for its optimistic vision of the future.

A movie is a form of visual storytelling that uses moving images and sound to entertain, educate, or inspire. Movies are typically 90-180 minutes long and are shown in theaters, on streaming platforms, or on television. The film industry produces thousands of movies annually worldwide.
